title: AI-Driven Resume Quality & ATS Analysis System
description: Built an end-to-end agentic resume tailoring system that ingests resume, GitHub, and LinkedIn data into a skills knowledge graph, then orchestrates a pipeline of LLM agents (via LangGraph and Claude/GPT-4) to analyze job descriptions, plan per-item edit actions, generate ATS-optimized one-page resumes, and iteratively score outputs against algorithmic checks. The system exposes a React/TypeScript chat interface backed by a FastAPI server, enabling users to propose, review, and approve targeted revisions in a structured feedback loop, with all tailoring decisions logged to a PostgreSQL decision store for explainability and future learning. Deployed to Railway with PDF export via LaTeX and DOCX generation, the system handles the full pipeline from raw profile data to formatted, job-specific resume artifacts.

title: Portfolio
description: Built a personal portfolio website to showcase data science projects, experience, and skills, serving as a live professional presence at nathansso.github.io. Implemented with vanilla HTML, CSS, and ES module JavaScript — no framework, bundler, or build step — keeping the architecture as a flat collection of static files deployable on any host. Automated GitHub repository metadata sync via custom Node.js scripts that fetch and merge project data into a single source-of-truth data layer without overwriting manually authored content.

title: Atrium.
description: Atrium is a full-stack AI learning platform that automatically generates cited, sequenced curricula from a single search query by crawling and evaluating live web sources via Firecrawl, then binding every claim to a ranked citation. The system runs each lesson through a simulated classroom of AI student personas, identifies failure points by learner type, and iteratively rewrites lesson content before any human student encounters it — all coordinated through an 11-event contract across a Next.js frontend, graph memory layer (FalkorDB), and multi-agent pipeline built on RocketRide. Atrium won 1st Place Overall at the Devnovate hackathon at Frontier Tower, San Francisco.

title: Job_Tracker
description: Built an automated job tracking pipeline that scrapes and scores early-apply New Grad 2027 and internship postings across six technical tracks — software engineering, data science, data engineering, machine learning & AI, AI engineering, and data analytics — filtering results against a Data Science major profile with June or December 2027 graduation eligibility. The system uses Playwright-driven browser scraping across ~60 Workday boards plus additional aggregators, parallel JD fetching, and a multi-factor matching engine that scores each role against an ingested resume profile before syncing strong-fit results to Notion and Discord. A Windows Scheduled Task runs the full pipeline twice daily, delivering ranked job lists, morning digests, and unapplied-role nag alerts through a self-contained HTML dashboard.

title: Alongside
description: Alongside was a longitudinal treatment companion for cancer patients that used a persistent Jac graph to track daily check-ins, medications, and symptoms across fragmented care settings. Rather than similarity-based retrieval, relevance was defined by graph reachability, enabling a mandatory traversal gate that blocked unsafe drug interactions before a new substance entered the regimen and surfaced unprompted concerns each time the app opened. The system translated accumulated graph findings into a patient-facing "Questions for your care team" page, with every flagged item cited back to the exact sentence that generated it.

title: Neetcode Submissions
description: Built a repository of coding interview solutions synced automatically from NeetCode.io using the platform's GitHub integration feature. Solutions span core data structures and algorithm topics, implemented in Python and organized by problem category for easy reference. The repository serves as a structured record of problem-solving practice, demonstrating proficiency across patterns such as binary search, dynamic programming, and graph traversal.

title: RollAway
description: RollAway was a map-first progressive web app built exclusively for San Francisco mobile food vendors, ranking legal vending locations by competition density, travel time, and regulatory compliance using deterministic scoring algorithms grounded in SF Public Works Order 182101 and live DataSF permit feeds. The system encoded SF's four-agency permit process (Public Works, DPH, Fire, and Treasurer) into a single guided checklist, while foot traffic signals were derived from a full year of Bay Wheels bike-share trip history aggregated by station, day-of-week, and hour. LLMs were scoped strictly to natural-language explanation generation, with all hard constraints — 75-ft restaurant setbacks, 500-ft school buffers, sidewalk width checks — computed in code and cited to source documents stored in a structured knowledge base.

title: AI Agent Policy Optimization
description: Built a reinforcement learning policy optimizer for an AI-driven HVAC contractor follow-up system, training an agent to select among seven discrete actions (e.g., CHECK_IN, ESTIMATE_NUDGE, ESCALATE, OPT_OUT) based on homeowner conversation state using a custom simulation environment written in pure Python. Designed a reward function that balanced conversion outcomes against opt-out risk, customer trust, and unnecessary contact cost, reflecting real business constraints across objection-handling and membership renewal scenarios. Evaluated the learned policy against rule-based baselines across simulated episode rollouts, demonstrating improved trade-offs between follow-up conversion rates and customer disengagement risk.

title: Diginetica: GNN vs. Flat Ranker for Session Recommendation
description: Built an end-to-end relational deep learning pipeline on the Diginetica (CIKM Cup 2016) e-commerce logs, using RelBench to convert the relational database into a heterogeneous graph — 8 node types (items, sessions, users plus view/query/click/queried-item/purchase events) and 22 edge types over 11 foreign-key relations. Engineered an `abs_time` event clock at microsecond resolution by folding intra-session millisecond offsets into the event date, enabling time-aware neighbor sampling that admits only neighbors strictly earlier than a per-row seed time so the receptive field never peeks at the future. Defined two tasks: session-conversion entity classification (binary, ~4% positive rate, AUPRC/AUROC) and next-item link prediction via intra-session leave-last-out on 218K sessions. The GNN is a two-tower heterogeneous GraphSAGE encoder (HeteroEncoder + temporal encoder) splitting into session and item towers scored by dot product, trained with sampled-softmax over in-batch and pool negatives. It is compared against an XGBoost LambdaRank ranker (`rank:ndcg`) over anchor-based 1-hop features — co-view, co-purchase, transition, category, popularity, price, is_repeat. A shared per-row candidate pool (co-view + transition + co-purchase + category + popularity backfill, built on train statistics only) lets both models rank the identical set, isolating ranking quality from candidate recall, with Optuna sweeps (persistent SQLite, median pruning) tuning both on Novel Recall@10. Evaluation decomposes Recall@10, NDCG@10, and MRR across slices — Repeat/Novel, popularity (Head/Torso/Tail), and session length — through a single masked `task.evaluate` code path, alongside structural ablations on hop depth, item-feature capacity, and scoring head (pooled dot vs. maxpool vs. ColBERT-style late interaction).

title: Idx_cont_training
description: Built an end-to-end MLOps pipeline for continuously training machine learning models on real estate listing data, incorporating automated data streaming to keep models updated with fresh market information. The pipeline integrated geospatial feature engineering with GeoPandas, ensemble modeling with LightGBM and XGBoost, and custom preprocessing modules for handling missing data and outliers. Model training and serialization were managed with scikit-learn and Joblib, enabling reproducible, production-ready deployment of property valuation models.

title: Portfolio Live Editor
description: Built an Express.js proxy server that intercepted live HTTP responses from a personal portfolio site and injected a WYSIWYG editing overlay into every served page, enabling point-and-click content editing directly on the rendered site. The overlay communicated with a custom REST API to read and write changes to a source JSON data file in real time, bypassing any build pipeline or recompilation step. This replaced manual source file edits with an in-place visual interface, eliminating context-switching between the live site and raw data files during content iteration.

title: Real Time ML Feature Store And Quant Research Platform
description: Built a modular, end-to-end quantitative research platform in Python that ingests daily OHLCV data for S&P 500 equities via Yahoo Finance, stores it in Parquet files queryable through DuckDB, and supports lot-level position tracking, wash-sale-aware tax-loss harvesting rules, and event-driven backtesting. Engineered a Feast-backed feature store to compute and serve financial signals, then trained a mean-reversion classifier to gate tax-loss harvesting decisions. The system was structured as six sequentially deployable phases, each independently tested with pytest, enabling clean separation between data ingestion, portfolio state management, strategy logic, and ML inference.

title: eCommerce Session Review Analysis - Predicting Online Shopper Purchase Intent
description: Built classification models using Random Forest and XGBoost on 12,330 e-commerce browsing sessions to predict purchase intent, applying threshold tuning to maximize recall and reduce missed conversions, achieving approximately 90% accuracy. Applied K-Means clustering to segment shoppers into five behavioral archetypes, uncovering conversion rates ranging from 0.4% for bounce-prone visitors to 24.3% for high-intent consumers. Identified product browsing depth and administrative page engagement as the strongest purchase predictors using Python, scikit-learn, pandas, and seaborn.
